questions.text: Let $f$ and $g$ be functions satisfying $f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)$, $f(1)=7$ and $g(x+y)=g(xy)$, $g(1)=1$, for all $x, y\in\mathbf{N}$. If $\displaystyle\sum_{x=1}^{n}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right)=19607$, then n is equal to :
questions.sol:
$f(x)=7^x$ on $\mathbf{N}$.
$g(2)=g(1+1)=g(1)=1$, and $g(n+1)=g(n\cdot1)=g(n)$, so $g(x)=1$ for all $x$.
$\sum_{x=1}^n7^x=\dfrac{7(7^n-1)}{6}=19607\Rightarrow7^n-1=16806\Rightarrow7^n=16807=7^5$, so $n=5$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the quadratic equation $12x^2-20x+3\lambda=0$, $\lambda\in\mathbf{Z}$. If $\dfrac12\le|\beta-\alpha|\le\dfrac32$, then the sum of all possible values of $\lambda$ is :
questions.sol:
$|\beta-\alpha|=\dfrac{\sqrt{400-144\lambda}}{12}$.
$\dfrac12\le\dfrac{\sqrt{400-144\lambda}}{12}\le\dfrac32\Rightarrow36\le400-144\lambda\le324\Rightarrow\dfrac{76}{144}\le\lambda\le\dfrac{364}{144}$.
Integers: $\lambda=1, 2$; sum $=3$.

questions.text: Let the domain of the function $f(x)=\log_3\log_5\left(7-\log_2\left(x^2-10x+85\right)\right)+\sin^{-1}\left(\left|\dfrac{3x-7}{17-x}\right|\right)$ be $(\alpha, \beta]$. Then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\log_3$ needs $\log_5(\ldots)>0$, i.e. $7-\log_2(x^2-10x+85)>1$, so $x^2-10x+85<64\Rightarrow(x-3)(x-7)<0\Rightarrow3<x<7$.
$\sin^{-1}$ needs $|3x-7|\le|17-x|$; on $(3,7)$ both are positive, so $3x-7\le17-x\Rightarrow x\le6$.
Domain $(3,6]$, so $\alpha+\beta=9$.

questions.text: Let $S=\{z\in\mathbb{C}: 4z^2+\bar{z}=0\}$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{z\in S}|z|^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Taking moduli: $4|z|^2=|z|$, so $z=0$ or $|z|=\dfrac14$.
If $|z|=\dfrac14$ then $\bar z=\dfrac{1}{16z}$, and $4z^2+\dfrac{1}{16z}=0\Rightarrow z^3=-\dfrac{1}{64}$: three distinct roots, each with $|z|^2=\dfrac{1}{16}$.
$\sum|z|^2=0+3\cdot\dfrac1{16}=\dfrac{3}{16}$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}$ is a solution of the system of equations $AX=B$, where $\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}4&2&2\\-5&0&5\\1&-2&3\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}4\\0\\2\end{bmatrix}$, then $|x+y+z|$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$|\operatorname{adj}A|=4(0+10)-2(-15-5)+2(10-0)=100=|A|^2$, so $|A|=\pm10$.
$X=\dfrac{1}{|A|}(\operatorname{adj}A)B=\dfrac{1}{|A|}\begin{bmatrix}20\\-10\\10\end{bmatrix}$.
$|x+y+z|=\dfrac{20}{10}=2$.

questions.text:
Let n be the number obtained on rolling a fair die. If the probability that the system
$x-ny+z=6$
$x+(n-2)y+(n+1)z=8$
$(n-1)y+z=1$
has a unique solution is $\dfrac{k}{6}$, then the sum of k and all possible values of n is :
questions.sol:
$\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}1&-n&1\\1&n-2&n+1\\0&n-1&1\end{vmatrix}=(n-2)-(n^2-1)+n+(n-1)=-(n-1)(n-2)$.
A unique solution needs $\Delta\ne0$: $n=3,4,5,6$, so $k=4$.
Sum $=4+3+4+5+6=22$.

questions.text: If the mean deviation about the median of the numbers $k, 2k, 3k, \ldots, 1000k$ is 500, then $k^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Median $=\dfrac{500k+501k}{2}=500.5k$ (taking $k>0$).
$\sum|ik-500.5k|=2k\sum_{j=1}^{500}(j-0.5)=2k\left(\dfrac{500\cdot501}{2}-250\right)=250000k$.
Mean deviation $=\dfrac{250000k}{1000}=250k=500\Rightarrow k=2$, so $k^2=4$.

questions.text: Let S and S$'$ be the foci of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1$ and $P(\alpha, \beta)$ be a point on the ellipse in the first quadrant. If $(SP)^2+(S'P)^2-SP\cdot S'P=37$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$a=5$, $e=\dfrac45$, and $SP+S'P=10$.
$(SP+S'P)^2-3\,SP\cdot S'P=37\Rightarrow SP\cdot S'P=21$.
$SP\cdot S'P=(5-e\alpha)(5+e\alpha)=25-\dfrac{16}{25}\alpha^2=21\Rightarrow\alpha^2=\dfrac{25}{4}$.
$\beta^2=9\left(1-\dfrac14\right)=\dfrac{27}{4}$, so $\alpha^2+\beta^2=13$.

questions.text: Let $P(10, 2\sqrt{15})$ be a point on the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, whose foci are S and S$'$. If the length of its latus rectum is 8, then the square of the area of $\Delta PSS'$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=8\Rightarrow b^2=4a$. P on the curve: $\dfrac{100}{a^2}-\dfrac{60}{4a}=1\Rightarrow a^2+15a-100=0\Rightarrow a=5$, $b^2=20$.
$c^2=a^2+b^2=45$, $c=3\sqrt5$, so $SS'=6\sqrt5$.
Area $=\dfrac12\cdot6\sqrt5\cdot2\sqrt{15}=30\sqrt3$; its square is $2700$.

questions.text: Let the locus of the mid-point of the chord through the origin O of the parabola $y^2=4x$ be the curve S. Let P be any point on S. Then the locus of the point, which internally divides OP in the ratio $3:1$, is :
questions.sol:
A chord from O to $(t^2, 2t)$ has mid-point $\left(\dfrac{t^2}{2}, t\right)$, so S is $y^2=2x$.
For $P(h,k)$ on S, the point dividing OP in $3:1$ is $(X,Y)=\left(\dfrac{3h}{4},\dfrac{3k}{4}\right)$.
$k^2=2h\Rightarrow\dfrac{16Y^2}{9}=\dfrac{8X}{3}\Rightarrow2Y^2=3X$: the locus is $2y^2=3x$.

questions.text:
Among the statements
(S1) : If $A(5, -1)$ and $B(-2, 3)$ are two vertices of a triangle, whose orthocentre is $(0, 0)$, then its third vertex is $(-4, -7)$
and
(S2) : If positive numbers $2a$, $b$, $c$ are three consecutive terms of an A.P., then the lines $ax+by+c=0$ are concurrent at $(2, -2)$,
questions.sol:
(S1): with $C(-4,-7)$, $\overrightarrow{BC}=(-2,-10)$ is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{OA}=(5,-1)$, and $\overrightarrow{AC}=(-9,-6)$ is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{OB}=(-2,3)$. So O is the orthocentre. Correct.
(S2): $2b=2a+c\Rightarrow2a-2b+c=0$, so every such line passes through $(2,-2)$. Correct.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\lambda\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $\lambda\in\mathbf{Z}$ be two vectors. Let $\vec{c}=\vec{a}\times\vec{b}$ and $\vec{d}$ be a vector of magnitude 2 in $yz$-plane. If $|\vec{c}|=\sqrt{53}$, then the maximum possible value of $\left(\vec{c}\cdot\vec{d}\right)^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\vec{c}=\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=(-2-\lambda)\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+2\lambda\hat{k}$.
$|\vec{c}|^2=(\lambda+2)^2+16+4\lambda^2=53\Rightarrow5\lambda^2+4\lambda-33=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-3$ (integer root).
$\vec{c}=\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-6\hat{k}$. For $\vec d$ in the $yz$-plane, $\vec c\cdot\vec d$ uses only $(-4,-6)$, of length $\sqrt{52}$.
Maximum $(\vec c\cdot\vec d)^2=52\times4=208$.

questions.text: Let L be the line $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{3}=\dfrac{z+3}{6}$ and let S be the set of all points $(a, b, c)$ on L, whose distance from the line $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{3}=\dfrac{z-9}{0}$ along the line L is 7. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{(a, b, c)\in S}(a+b+c)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Points of L: $(-1+2t, -1+3t, -3+6t)$; the direction $(2,3,6)$ has length 7, so a change of 1 in $t$ moves 7 units.
L meets the second line (where $z=9$) at $t=2$: $(3,5,9)$, which satisfies $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{3}=2$.
Points 7 units away along L: $t=3$, $(5,8,15)$, sum 28; $t=1$, $(1,2,3)$, sum 6.
Total $=34$.

questions.text: Let $[\cdot]$ denote the greatest integer function, and let $f(x)=\min\{\sqrt2x, x^2\}$. Let $S=\{x\in(-2, 2):$ the function $g(x)=|x|[x^2]$ is discontinuous at $x\}$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{x\in S}f(x)$ equals
questions.sol:
$[x^2]$ jumps where $x^2=1,2,3$, i.e. $x=\pm1,\pm\sqrt2,\pm\sqrt3$; there $|x|\ne0$, so $g$ is discontinuous. (At $x=0$, $g$ is continuous.)
For $x>0$: $f(1)=1$, $f(\sqrt2)=2$, $f(\sqrt3)=\min(\sqrt6,3)=\sqrt6$.
For $x<0$, $\sqrt2x<0<x^2$: $f=-\sqrt2,-2,-\sqrt6$.
Sum $=1+2+\sqrt6-\sqrt2-2-\sqrt6=1-\sqrt2$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{e^{(a-1)x}+2\cos bx+(c-2)e^{-x}}{x\cos x-\log_e(1+x)}=2$, then $a^2+b^2+c^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Denominator: $x\left(1-\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)-\left(x-\dfrac{x^2}{2}+\ldots\right)=\dfrac{x^2}{2}+O(x^3)$.
So the numerator must start at $x^2$: constant term $1+2+c-2=0\Rightarrow c=-1$; $x$ term $(a-1)+3=0\Rightarrow a=-2$.
Numerator $=e^{-3x}+2\cos bx-3e^{-x}$, whose $x^2$ coefficient is $\dfrac92-b^2-\dfrac32=3-b^2$.
Limit $=\dfrac{3-b^2}{1/2}=2\Rightarrow b^2=2$. Hence $a^2+b^2+c^2=4+2+1=7$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f(x)=[x]^2-[x+3]-3$, $x\in\mathbf{R}$, where $[\cdot]$ is the greatest integer funtion. Then
questions.sol:
With $n=[x]$: $f=n^2-(n+3)-3=n^2-n-6=(n-3)(n+2)$.
$f=0$ for $n=3$ or $n=-2$, i.e. on whole intervals: infinitely many $x$. $f<0$ for $n=-1,0,1,2$, i.e. exactly $x\in[-1,3)$. $f>0$ also for $x<-2$.
$\int_0^2f=(-6)+(-6)=-12$.
Only the second statement is true.

questions.text: The area of the region $A=\{(x, y): 4x^2+y^2\le8$ and $y^2\le4x\}$ is :
questions.sol:
The curves meet where $4x^2+4x=8$, i.e. $x=1$, $y=\pm2$. By symmetry about the $x$-axis:
Area $=2\left[\displaystyle\int_0^1 2\sqrt{x}\,dx+\int_1^{\sqrt2}2\sqrt{2-x^2}\,dx\right]$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^12\sqrt x\,dx=\dfrac43$; $\displaystyle\int_1^{\sqrt2}\sqrt{2-x^2}\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\left(\dfrac12+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac12$.
Area $=2\left[\dfrac43+\dfrac{\pi}{2}-1\right]=\pi+\dfrac23$.

questions.text:
If $y=y(x)$ satisfies the differential equation
$16\left(\sqrt{x+9\sqrt{x}}\right)\left(4+\sqrt{9+\sqrt{x}}\right)\cos y\,dy=(1+2\sin y)\,dx$, $x>0$ and $y(256)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $y(49)=\alpha$, then $2\sin\alpha$ is equal to :
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone. As printed, the first factor is the square root of (x + 9 root x), which does not lead to a closed-form answer; reading it as root x times root(9 + root x) gives 2 sin(alpha) = 2 root 2 - 1, the first option.
questions.sol:
As printed, $\sqrt{x+9\sqrt x}=x^{1/4}\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}$, and the equation does not separate into a form that gives a listed value.
Reading the factor as $\sqrt x\,\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}$: put $t=\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}$, so $dx=4t\sqrt x\,dt$.
$\dfrac{\cos y\,dy}{1+2\sin y}=\dfrac{4t\sqrt x\,dt}{16\sqrt x\,t(4+t)}=\dfrac{dt}{4(4+t)}\Rightarrow\dfrac12\ln(1+2\sin y)=\dfrac14\ln(4+t)+C$.
$x=256$: $t=5$, $y=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ gives $\dfrac12\ln3=\dfrac14\ln9+C$, so $C=0$.
$x=49$: $t=4$, so $1+2\sin\alpha=\sqrt8$ and $2\sin\alpha=2\sqrt2-1$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Suppose $a, b, c$ are in A.P. and $a^2, 2b^2, c^2$ are in G.P. If $a<b<c$ and $a+b+c=1$, then $9(a^2+b^2+c^2)$ is equal to ___________.
questions.sol:
$3b=1\Rightarrow b=\dfrac13$; write $a=\dfrac13-d$, $c=\dfrac13+d$ with $d>0$.
G.P.: $4b^4=a^2c^2\Rightarrow|ac|=2b^2=\dfrac29$, with $ac=\dfrac19-d^2$. Since $\dfrac19-d^2=\dfrac29$ is impossible, $d^2-\dfrac19=\dfrac29$, so $d^2=\dfrac13$.
$a^2+b^2+c^2=3b^2+2d^2=\dfrac13+\dfrac23=1$, so $9(a^2+b^2+c^2)=9$.

questions.text: Let S be the set of the first 11 natural numbers. Then the number of elements in $A=\{B\subseteq S: n(B)\ge2$ and the product of all elements of B is even$\}$ is ___________.
questions.sol:
Subsets with at least 2 elements: $2^{11}-1-11=2036$.
The product is odd only if all elements are odd; with 6 odd numbers, such subsets of size at least 2 number $2^6-1-6=57$.
$2036-57=1979$.

questions.text: Let $\cos(\alpha+\beta)=-\dfrac{1}{10}$ and $\sin(\alpha-\beta)=\dfrac38$, where $0<\alpha<\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $0<\beta<\dfrac{\pi}{4}$. If $\tan2\alpha=\dfrac{3(1-r\sqrt5)}{\sqrt{11}(s+\sqrt5)}$, $r, s\in\mathbf{N}$, then $r+s$ is equal to ___________.
questions.sol:
$\alpha+\beta\in\left(0,\dfrac{7\pi}{12}\right)$, so $\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\dfrac{3\sqrt{11}}{10}$ and $\tan(\alpha+\beta)=-3\sqrt{11}$.
$\alpha-\beta\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4},\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$, so $\cos(\alpha-\beta)=\dfrac{\sqrt{55}}{8}$ and $\tan(\alpha-\beta)=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{55}}$.
$\tan2\alpha=\dfrac{-3\sqrt{11}+\frac{3}{\sqrt{55}}}{1+\frac{9\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt{55}}}=\dfrac{3-33\sqrt5}{\sqrt{55}+9\sqrt{11}}=\dfrac{3(1-11\sqrt5)}{\sqrt{11}(9+\sqrt5)}$.
So $r=11$, $s=9$, and $r+s=20$.

questions.text: Let a vector $\vec{a}=\sqrt2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}$, $\lambda>0$, make an obtuse angle with the vector $\vec{b}=-\lambda^2\hat{i}+4\sqrt2\hat{j}+4\sqrt2\hat{k}$ and an angle $\theta$, $\dfrac{\pi}{6}<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, with the positive $z$-axis. If the set of all possible values of $\lambda$ is $(\alpha, \beta)-\{\gamma\}$, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to ___________.
questions.sol:
Obtuse angle: $\vec a\cdot\vec b=-\sqrt2\lambda^2-4\sqrt2+4\sqrt2\lambda<0\iff(\lambda-2)^2>0\iff\lambda\ne2$.
Angle with the $z$-axis: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3+\lambda^2}}\in\left(0,\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\Rightarrow4\lambda^2<9+3\lambda^2\Rightarrow\lambda<3$.
So $\lambda\in(0,3)-\{2\}$ and $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=0+3+2=5$.

questions.text: Let $[\cdot]$ be the greatest integer function. If $\alpha=\displaystyle\int_0^{64}\left(x^{1/3}-[x^{1/3}]\right)dx$, then $\dfrac{1}{\pi}\displaystyle\int_0^{\alpha\pi}\left(\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^6\theta+\cos^6\theta}\right)d\theta$ is equal to _________.
questions.sol:
$\displaystyle\int_0^{64}x^{1/3}dx=\dfrac34\cdot64^{4/3}=192$. $[x^{1/3}]$ is 1 on $[1,8)$, 2 on $[8,27)$, 3 on $[27,64)$: $\displaystyle\int_0^{64}[x^{1/3}]dx=7+38+111=156$. So $\alpha=36$.
The integrand has period $\pi$. On $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ put $t=\tan\theta$: $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^6\theta+\cos^6\theta}d\theta=\int_0^\infty\dfrac{t^2(1+t^2)}{1+t^6}dt=\int_0^\infty\dfrac{t^2}{t^4-t^2+1}dt=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
(Substituting $t\to\dfrac1t$ shows this equals $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty\dfrac{dt}{t^4-t^2+1}$, and their sum is $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty\dfrac{d(t-1/t)}{(t-1/t)^2+1}=\pi$.)
Over one period the integral is $\pi$, so over $36\pi$ it is $36\pi$, and dividing by $\pi$ gives $36$.

questions.text: Using a simple pendulum experiment $g$ is determind by measuring its time period $T$. Which of the following plots represent the correct relation between the pendulum length $L$ and time period $T$?
questions.sol:
$T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}\Rightarrow\dfrac{1}{T^2}=\dfrac{g}{4\pi^2}\cdot\dfrac1L$.
So $\dfrac1{T^2}$ against $L$ is a rectangular hyperbola, falling steeply and then levelling off: the first graph.

questions.text: If $\epsilon$, $E$ and $t$ represent the free space permittivity, electric field and time respectively, then the unit of $\dfrac{\epsilon E}{t}$ will be :
questions.sol:
$\epsilon E$ has the unit of surface charge density, C/m$^2$ (from Gauss's law, $E=\dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon}$).
Dividing by time: C s$^{-1}$ m$^{-2}$ = A/m$^2$ (the displacement current density).

questions.text: A uniform bar of length 12 cm and mass 20 $m$ lies on a smooth horizontal table. Two point masses $m$ and $2m$ are moving in opposite directions with same speed of $v$ and in the same plane as the bar, as shown in figure. These masses strike the bar simultaneously and get stuck to it. After collision the entire system is rotating with angular frequency $\omega$. The ratio of $v$ and $\omega$ is :
questions.sol:
Measure positions from the centre of the bar: $2m$ strikes 2 cm to one side and $m$ 4 cm to the other side.
Centre of mass after impact: $\dfrac{2m(-2)+m(4)}{23m}=0$, the centre of the bar.
Angular momentum about it (both masses turn the bar the same way): $2mv(2)+mv(4)=8mv$.
$I=\dfrac{20m(12)^2}{12}+2m(2)^2+m(4)^2=240m+8m+16m=264m$ (cm$^2$).
$\omega=\dfrac{8mv}{264m}=\dfrac{v}{33}$, so $\dfrac{v}{\omega}=33$ (in cm).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : An object moves from position $r_1$ to position $r_2$ under a conservative force field $\vec{F}$. The work done by the force is $W=-\displaystyle\int_{r_1}^{r_2}\vec{F}\cdot\vec{dr}$.
Statement II : Any object moving from one location to another location can follow infinite number of paths. Therefore, the amount of work done by the object changes with the path it follows for a conservative force.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: the work done by the force is $+\displaystyle\int_{r_1}^{r_2}\vec F\cdot d\vec r$; the expression with the minus sign is the change in potential energy. False.
Statement II: for a conservative force the work depends only on the end points, not on the path. False.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : For a mechanical system of many particles total kinetic energy is the sum of kinetic energies of all the particles.
Statement II : The total kinetic energy can be the sum of kinetic energy of the center of mass w.r.t to the origin and the kinetic energy of all the particles w.r.t. the center of mass as the reference.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is true: kinetic energy is a scalar, so the total is the sum over the particles.
Statement II is true: writing $\vec v_i=\vec V_{cm}+\vec v_i'$ and using $\sum m_i\vec v_i'=0$ gives $K=\dfrac12MV_{cm}^2+\sum\dfrac12m_iv_i'^2$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : A satellite is moving around earth in the orbit very close to the earth surface. The time period of revolution of satellite depends upon the density of earth.
Statement II : The time period of revolution of the satellite is $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R_e}{g}}$ (for satellite very close to the earth surface), where $R_e$ radius of earth and $g$ acceleration due to gravity.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
For an orbit just above the surface, $\dfrac{mv^2}{R_e}=mg$, so $T=\dfrac{2\pi R_e}{v}=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R_e}{g}}$. Statement II is true.
With $g=\dfrac43\pi G\rho R_e$, $T=\sqrt{\dfrac{3\pi}{G\rho}}$, which depends on the density. Statement I is true.

questions.text: When a part of a straight capillary tube is placed vertically in a liquid, the liquid raises upto certain height $h$. If the inner radius of the capillary tube, density of the liquid and surface tension of the liquid decrease by 1% each, then the height of the liquid in the tube will change by ______ %.
questions.sol:
$h=\dfrac{2S\cos\theta}{r\rho g}$, so for small changes $\dfrac{\Delta h}{h}=\dfrac{\Delta S}{S}-\dfrac{\Delta r}{r}-\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}$.
$=-1\%+1\%+1\%=+1\%$.

questions.text: Three small identical bubbles of water having same charge on each coalesce to form a bigger bubble. Then the ratio of the potentials on one initial bubble and that on the resultant bigger bubble is :
questions.sol:
Treat each as a charged sphere (drop) of radius $r$: $V=\dfrac{kq}{r}$.
Volume is conserved: $R=3^{1/3}r$; the charge becomes $3q$.
$V'=\dfrac{k(3q)}{3^{1/3}r}=3^{2/3}V$, so the ratio is $1:3^{2/3}$.

questions.text: Figure shows the circuit that contains three resistances (9 $\Omega$ each) and two inductors (4 mH each). The reading of ammeter at the moment switch $K$ is turned ON, is __________A.
questions.sol:
At the instant the switch is closed, an inductor carries no current (it opposes any sudden change), so both branches containing an inductor act as open circuits.
Only the middle $9\ \Omega$ branch conducts: $I=\dfrac{9}{9}=1$ A, which is the ammeter reading.

questions.text: Consider two boxes containing ideal gases $A$ and $B$ such that their temperatures, pressures and number densities are same. The molecular size of $A$ is half of that of $B$ and mass of molecule $A$ is four times that of $B$. If the collision frequency in gas $B$ is $32\times10^{18}$/s then collision frequency in gas $A$ is __________/s.
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone. The working gives 4 x 10^18 /s, while the options are printed with 10^8.
questions.sol:
Collision frequency $f=\sqrt2\pi d^2nv_{\text{avg}}$, with $v_{\text{avg}}\propto\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{m}}$; $n$ and $T$ are the same.
$\dfrac{f_A}{f_B}=\left(\dfrac{d_A}{d_B}\right)^2\sqrt{\dfrac{m_B}{m_A}}=\dfrac14\cdot\dfrac12=\dfrac18$.
$f_A=\dfrac{32\times10^{18}}{8}=4\times10^{18}$/s. The options carry $10^8$ instead of $10^{18}$, so none matches exactly.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In an open organ pipe $ u_3$ and $ u_6$ are 3$^{ ext{rd}}$ and 6$^{ ext{th}}$ harmonic frequencies, respectively. If $ u_6- u_3=2200$ Hz then length of the pipe is __________ mm.
(Take velocity of sound in air is 330 m/s.)
questions.sol:
For an open pipe $ u_n=\dfrac{nv}{2L}$, so $ u_6- u_3=\dfrac{3v}{2L}=2200$.
$L=\dfrac{3 imes330}{2 imes2200}=0.225$ m $=225$ mm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Five positive charges each having charge $q$ are placed at the vertices of a pentagon as shown in the figure. The electric potential $(V)$ and the electric field $\left(\vec{E}\right)$ at the center $O$ of the pentagon due to these five positive charges are :
questions.sol:
Potential is a scalar, so the five equal contributions add: $V=\dfrac{5q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r}$.
The five field vectors have equal magnitude and point along directions $72^\circ$ apart, so they add to zero: $\vec E=0$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An electric power line having total resistance of 2 $\Omega$, delivers 1 kW of power at 250 V. The percentage efficiency of transmission line is _________.
questions.sol:
Current $I=\dfrac{P}{V}=\dfrac{1000}{250}=4$ A; loss in the line $=I^2R=16\times2=32$ W.
Efficiency $=\dfrac{1000}{1000+32}\times100\approx96.9\%$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A laser beam has intensity of $4.0\times10^{14}$ W/m$^2$. The amplitude of magnetic field associated with beam is ___________T. (Take $\epsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}$ C$^2$/Nm$^2$ and $c=3\times10^8$ m/s)
questions.sol:
$I=\dfrac{cB_0^2}{2\mu_0}$ with $\mu_0=\dfrac{1}{\epsilon_0c^2}$, so $B_0^2=\dfrac{2I}{\epsilon_0c^3}$.
$B_0^2=\dfrac{8.0\times10^{14}}{8.85\times10^{-12}\times2.7\times10^{25}}\approx3.35\Rightarrow B_0\approx1.83$ T.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The wavelength of light, while it is passing through water is 540 nm. The refractive index of water is $4/3$. The wavelength of the same light when it is passing through a transparent medium having refractive index of $3/2$ is _________ nm.
questions.sol:
The frequency does not change, so $\lambda\mu$ is constant: $540\times\dfrac43=\lambda\times\dfrac32$.
$\lambda=\dfrac{720}{1.5}=480$ nm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: In parallax method for the determination of focal length of a concave mirror, the object should always be placed :
options: between the pole($P$) and the focus($F$) of the concave mirror ONLY
between the focus($F$) and the centre of curvature($C$) of the mirror ONLY
beyond the centre of the curvature($C$) of the mirror ONLY
at any point beyond the focus($F$) of the mirror
questions.sol:
The parallax method locates a real image with a second pin (removing parallax between the image and the pin).
A concave mirror forms a real image for any object position beyond the focus, so the object pin may be placed anywhere beyond F. Between P and F the image is virtual and cannot be located on the pin in this way.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Which of the following are true for a single slit diffraction ?
A. Width of central maxima increases with increase in wavelength keeping slit width constant.
B. Width of central maxima increases with decrease in wavelength keeping slit width constant.
C. Width of central maxima increases with decrease in slit width at constant wavelength.
D. Width of central maxima increases with increase in slit width at constant wavelength.
E. Brightness of central maxima increases for decrease in wavelength at constant slit width.
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone. The true statements are A and C (with E arguable), and no option gives that combination.
questions.sol:
Angular width of the central maximum $=\dfrac{2\lambda}{a}$.
It grows with $\lambda$ (A true, B false) and as the slit width $a$ decreases (C true, D false).
A smaller $\lambda$ narrows the central maximum and concentrates the light, so E can be argued either way.
Every option includes B or D, which are false, so no option is correct.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Light is incident on a metallic plate having work function $110\times10^{-20}$ J. If the produced photoelectrons have zero kinetic energy then the angular frequency of the incident light is ________rad/s. ($h=6.63\times10^{-34}$ J.s).
questions.sol:
Zero kinetic energy means the photon energy equals the work function: $h u=1.1 imes10^{-18}$ J.
$ u=\dfrac{1.1 imes10^{-18}}{6.63 imes10^{-34}}\approx1.66 imes10^{15}$ Hz.
$\omega=2\pi u\approx1.04 imes10^{16}$ rad/s.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: The smallest wavelength of Lyman series is 91 nm. The difference between the largest wavelengths of Paschen and Balmer series is nearly ______ nm.
questions.sol:
Lyman limit: $\dfrac1{91\ \text{nm}}=R$.
Largest Paschen ($4\to3$): $\dfrac1\lambda=R\left(\dfrac19-\dfrac1{16}\right)=\dfrac{7R}{144}\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac{144\times91}{7}=1872$ nm.
Largest Balmer ($3\to2$): $\dfrac1\lambda=\dfrac{5R}{36}\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac{36\times91}{5}=655.2$ nm.
Difference $\approx1217$ nm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The correct truth table for the given input data of the following logic gate is :
questions.sol:
A and B pass through AND then NOT: $P=\overline{AB}$. C and D pass through OR: $Q=C+D$.
P and Q pass through AND then NOT: $Y=\overline{P\cdot Q}$.
1101: $P=0\Rightarrow Y=1$. 0011: $P=1$, $Q=1\Rightarrow Y=0$. 1010: $P=1$, $Q=1\Rightarrow Y=0$. 1111: $P=0\Rightarrow Y=1$.
Outputs 1, 0, 0, 1: the third table.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two masses $m$ and $2m$ are connected by a light string going over a pulley (disc) of mass $30m$ with radius $r=0.1$ m. The pulley is mounted in a vertical plane and it is free to rotate about its axis. The $2m$ mass is released from rest and its speed when it has descended through a height of 3.6 m is ___________ m/s. (Assume string does not slip and $g=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
Energy conservation: loss of potential energy $=2mgh-mgh=mgh$.
Kinetic energy $=\dfrac12(3m)v^2+\dfrac12\left(\dfrac12\cdot30m\,r^2\right)\dfrac{v^2}{r^2}=1.5mv^2+7.5mv^2=9mv^2$.
$9v^2=gh=36\Rightarrow v=2$ m/s.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: A capacitor $P$ with capacitance $10\times10^{-6}$ F is fully charged with a potential difference of 6.0 V and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor $P$ is connected across another capacitor $Q$ with capacitance $20\times10^{-6}$ F. The charge on capacitor $Q$ when equilibrium is established will be $\alpha\times10^{-5}$ C (assume capacitor $Q$ does not have any charge initially), the value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Initial charge $=10\times10^{-6}\times6=60\ \mu$C, shared at a common potential $V=\dfrac{60\ \mu\text{C}}{30\ \mu\text{F}}=2$ V.
Charge on Q $=20\ \mu\text{F}\times2\ \text{V}=40\ \mu$C $=4\times10^{-5}$ C, so $\alpha=4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A cylindrical conductor of length 2 m and area of cross-section 0.2 mm$^2$ carries an electric current of 1.6 A when its ends are connected to a 2 V battery. Mobility of electrons in the conductor is $\alpha\times10^{-3}$ m$^2$/V.s. The value of $\alpha$ is :
(electron concentration = $5\times10^{28}$/m$^3$ and electron charge = $1.6\times10^{-19}$ C)
questions.sol:
$I=neA\mu E$ with $E=\dfrac{V}{L}=1$ V/m.
$\mu=\dfrac{I}{neAE}=\dfrac{1.6}{5\times10^{28}\times1.6\times10^{-19}\times0.2\times10^{-6}\times1}=\dfrac{1.6}{1.6\times10^{3}}=1\times10^{-3}$ m$^2$/V s, so $\alpha=1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An insulated cylinder of volume 60 cm$^3$ is filled with a gas at 27 °C and 2 atmospheric pressure. Then the gas is compressed making the final volume as 20 cm$^3$ while allowing the temperature to rise to 77 °C. The final pressure is __________ atmospheric pressure.
questions.sol: $\dfrac{p_1V_1}{T_1}=\dfrac{p_2V_2}{T_2}\Rightarrow p_2=2\times\dfrac{60}{20}\times\dfrac{350}{300}=7$ atm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A conducting circular loop is rotated about its diameter at a constant angular speed of 100 rad/s in a magnetic field of 0.5 T perpendicular to the axis of rotation. When the loop is rotated by $30^\circ$ from the horizontal position, the induced EMF is 15.4 mV. The radius of the loop is ________ mm.
$\left(\text{Take }\pi=\dfrac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.sol:
Taking the flux as greatest in the horizontal position, $\Phi=BA\cos\omega t$ and $\varepsilon=BA\omega\sin\omega t$.
At $30^\circ$: $15.4\times10^{-3}=0.5\times\pi r^2\times100\times\dfrac12=25\pi r^2$.
$r^2=\dfrac{15.4\times10^{-3}\times7}{25\times22}=1.96\times10^{-4}$ m$^2$, so $r=0.014$ m $=14$ mm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
$\mathrm{A+2B\longrightarrow AB_2}$
36.0 g of 'A' (Molar mass : 60 g mol$^{-1}$) and 56.0 g of 'B' (Molar mass : 80 g mol$^{-1}$) are allowed to react. Which of the following statements are correct ?
A. 'A' is the limiting reagent.
B. 77.0 g of $\mathrm{AB_2}$ is formed.
C. Molar mass of $\mathrm{AB_2}$ is 140 g mol$^{-1}$.
D. 15.0 g of A is left unreacted after the completion of reaction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: $\dfrac{36}{60}=0.6$ mol; B: $\dfrac{56}{80}=0.7$ mol. 0.7 mol B needs only 0.35 mol A, so B is limiting (A false).
$\mathrm{AB_2}$: 0.35 mol, molar mass $60+2\times80=220$ g mol$^{-1}$ (C false), mass $0.35\times220=77.0$ g (B true).
A left: $0.25$ mol $=15.0$ g (D true). Answer: B and D only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The energy of first (lowest) Balmer line of H atom is $x$ J. The energy (in J) of second Balmer line of H atom is :
questions.sol:
First Balmer line ($3\to2$): $E\propto\dfrac14-\dfrac19=\dfrac{5}{36}$. Second ($4\to2$): $\dfrac14-\dfrac1{16}=\dfrac{3}{16}$.
Ratio $=\dfrac{3/16}{5/36}=\dfrac{108}{80}=1.35$, so the energy is $1.35x$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
At T(K), 100 g of 98% $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ (w/w) aqueous solution is mixed with 100 g of 49% $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ (w/w) aqueous solution. What is the mole fraction of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ in the resultant solution ?
(Given : Atomic mass H = 1 u ; S = 32 u ; O = 16 u).
(Assume that temperature after mixing remains constant)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$: $98+49=147$ g $=1.5$ mol. Water: $2+51=53$ g $\approx2.944$ mol.
Mole fraction $=\dfrac{1.5}{1.5+2.944}\approx0.337$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which of the following mixture gives a buffer solution with pH = 9.25 ?
Given : $\mathrm{p}K_b\ (\mathrm{NH_4OH})=4.75$
questions.sol:
pH $9.25\Rightarrow$ pOH $=4.75=\mathrm{p}K_b$, so we need $[\mathrm{NH_4^+}]=[\mathrm{NH_4OH}]$: the acid must neutralise exactly half the base.
Option 3: 0.1 mol $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$ with 0.05 mol HCl leaves 0.05 mol of each. (Option 1 leaves 0.3 : 0.1; options 2 and 4 use up all the base.)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following reduction processes :
$\mathrm{Al^{3+}+3e^-\longrightarrow Al(s)}$, $E^\circ=-1.66$ V
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}+e^-\longrightarrow Fe^{2+}}$, $E^\circ=+0.77$ V
$\mathrm{Co^{3+}+e^-\longrightarrow Co^{2+}}$, $E^\circ=+1.81$ V
$\mathrm{Cr^{3+}+3e^-\longrightarrow Cr(s)}$, $E^\circ=-0.74$ V
The tendency to act as reducing agent decreases in the order :
questions.sol:
The lower the reduction potential, the stronger the reduced form is as a reducing agent.
$E^\circ$: Al $-1.66$ < Cr $-0.74$ < $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ $+0.77$ < $\mathrm{Co^{2+}}$ $+1.81$.
Order: $\mathrm{Al>Cr>Fe^{2+}>Co^{2+}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Correct statements regarding Arrhenius equation among the following are :
A. Factor $e^{-Ea/RT}$ corresponds to fraction of molecules having kinetic energy less than Ea.
B. At a given temperature, lower the Ea, faster is the reaction.
C. Increase in temperature by about 10°C doubles the rate of reaction.
D. Plot of log k vs $\dfrac1T$ gives a straight line with slope $=-\dfrac{Ea}{R}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: $e^{-E_a/RT}$ is the fraction of molecules with energy equal to or greater than $E_a$, not less. False.
B: a smaller $E_a$ gives a larger $k$ at a given temperature. True.
C: for many reactions a rise of about 10 °C roughly doubles the rate constant. True.
D: $\log k$ against $\dfrac1T$ has slope $-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303R}$ (slope $-\dfrac{E_a}{R}$ is for $\ln k$). False.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Among $\mathrm{H_2S}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{NF_3}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$, identify the molecule (X) with lowest dipole moment value. The number of lone pairs of electrons present on the central atom of the molecule (X) is :
questions.sol:
In $\mathrm{NF_3}$ the lone-pair moment on N opposes the resultant of the N-F bond moments, so its dipole moment (about 0.23 D) is the lowest of the five.
N in $\mathrm{NF_3}$ has one lone pair.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : C < O < N < F is the correct order in terms of first ionization enthalpy values.
Statement II : S > Se > Te > Po > O is the correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy values.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: C 1086, O 1314, N 1402, F 1681 kJ mol$^{-1}$; N is above O because of its half-filled 2p subshell. True.
Statement II: magnitudes S 200, Se 195, Te 190, Po about 174, O 141 kJ mol$^{-1}$; oxygen is lowest because its small size causes strong electron repulsion. True.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Elements 'X' and 'Y' are the most and least electronegative elements, respectively among N, As, Sb and P. The nature of the oxides $\mathrm{X_2O_3}$ and $\mathrm{Y_2O_3}$ is acidic and amphoteric, respectively.
Statement II : $\mathrm{BCl_3}$ is covalent in nature and gets hydrolysed in water. It produces $\mathrm{[B(OH)_4]^-}$ and $\mathrm{[B(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$ in aqueous medium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: X = N and Y = Sb. $\mathrm{N_2O_3}$ is acidic and $\mathrm{Sb_2O_3}$ is amphoteric (oxides become more basic down the group). True.
Statement II: $\mathrm{BCl_3}$ is covalent and hydrolyses to $\mathrm{B(OH)_3}$, which gives $\mathrm{[B(OH)_4]^-}$. Boron has no d orbitals and cannot exceed a covalency of 4, so $\mathrm{[B(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$ does not form. False.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The first ionization enthalpy of Cr is lower than that of Mn.
Statement II : The second and third ionization enthalpies of Cr are higher than those of Mn.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
First ionisation enthalpy: Cr 653, Mn 717 kJ mol$^{-1}$. Statement I is true.
Second: Cr 1592 > Mn 1509 (removing an electron from the stable $3d^5$ of $\mathrm{Cr^+}$). Third: Cr 2987 < Mn 3248 (for $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$, $3d^5$ is being broken). So the third is not higher for Cr. Statement II is false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$\mathrm{[Ni(PPh_3)_2Cl_2]}$ is a paramagnetic complex. Identify the INCORRECT statements about this complex.
A. The complex exhibits geometrical isomerism.
B. The complex is white in colour.
C. The calculated spin-only magnetic moment of the complex is 2.84 BM.
D. The calculated CFSE (Crystal Field Stabilization Energy) of Ni in this complex is $-0.8\,\Delta_o$.
E. The geometrical arrangement of ligands in this complex is similar to that in $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Paramagnetic $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ ($d^8$) with these ligands means a tetrahedral complex with 2 unpaired electrons.
A: tetrahedral $\mathrm{MA_2B_2}$ shows no geometrical isomerism. Incorrect.
B: with unpaired d electrons and d-d transitions the complex is coloured, not white. Incorrect.
C: $\sqrt{2(2+2)}=\sqrt8\approx2.83$ BM. Correct.
D: tetrahedral $e^4t_2^4$: CFSE $=(-0.6\times4+0.4\times4)\Delta_t=-0.8\Delta_t$, not $-0.8\Delta_o$. Incorrect.
E: $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ is also tetrahedral. Correct.
Incorrect statements: A, B and D.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the correct statements :
A. Hydrated salts can be used as primary standard.
B. Primary standard should not undergo any reaction with air.
C. Reactions of primary standard with another substance should be instantaneous and stoichiometric.
D. Primary standard should not be soluble in water.
E. Primary standard should have low relative molar mass.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A, B, C and E Only
questions.sol:
A: stable hydrated salts such as oxalic acid dihydrate and Mohr's salt are routinely used as primary standards. True.
B and C: a primary standard must be stable in air and must react rapidly and stoichiometrically. True.
D: it must dissolve in water to make the standard solution. False.
E: a high molar mass is preferred, to reduce weighing errors. False.
Correct: A, B and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: When 1 g of compound (X) is subjected to Kjeldahl's method for estimation of nitrogen, 15 mL 1 M $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ was neutralized by ammonia evolved. The percentage of nitrogen in compound (X) is :
questions.sol:
15 mmol of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ neutralise $2\times15=30$ mmol of $\mathrm{NH_3}$.
Nitrogen $=30\times10^{-3}\times14=0.42$ g in 1 g, i.e. $42\%$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the following compound is :
questions.sol:
It is an ester: the alkyl group on oxygen is n-propyl.
Acid chain from the carbonyl carbon: C1 (C=O), C2 (bears Br), C3, C4, C5 (branch point), then on through the ethyl branch, C6, C7; the remaining branch on C5 is a methyl.
Name: n-propyl 2-bromo-5-methylheptanoate.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction :
The product Y formed is :
questions.sol:
The starting compound is a dibromobutane with both bromines at the chain end. Two eliminations with $\mathrm{NaNH_2}$ give but-1-yne (X), $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2C\equiv CH}$.
$\mathrm{NaNH_2}$ forms the acetylide $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2C\equiv C^-}$, which is alkylated by 2-bromopropane.
Y $=\mathrm{CH_3CH_2C\equiv C{-}CH(CH_3)_2}$, i.e. 2-methylhex-3-yne.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The dibromo compound [P] (molecular formula : $\mathrm{C_9H_{10}Br_2}$) when heated with excess sodamide followed by treatment with dilute HCl gives [Q]. On warming [Q] with mercuric sulphate and dilute sulphuric acid yield [R] which gives positive Iodoform test but negative Tollen's test. The compound [P] is :
questions.sol:
Excess sodamide removes two HBr from a gem- or vic-dibromide (with H on the right carbons) to give an alkyne (as its sodium salt for a terminal alkyne; dilute HCl frees it).
For the second structure, $p\text{-}\mathrm{CH_3C_6H_4CBr_2CH_3}$ (formula $\mathrm{C_9H_{10}Br_2}$), Q is $p\text{-}\mathrm{CH_3C_6H_4C\equiv CH}$.
$\mathrm{HgSO_4}$/dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ hydrates it (Markovnikov) to $p\text{-}\mathrm{CH_3C_6H_4COCH_3}$, a methyl ketone: iodoform positive, Tollens' negative.
In the first structure the carbon carrying Br and $\mathrm{CH_3}$ has no H, so an alkyne cannot form; the third (two separate $\mathrm{CH_2Br}$ groups) cannot give an alkyne either. Only the second structure fits all the observations.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The compound A, $\mathrm{C_8H_8O_2}$ reacts with acetophenone to form a single product via cross-Aldol condensation. The compound A on reaction with conc. NaOH forms a substituted benzyl alcohol as one of the two products. The compound A is :
questions.sol:
A Cannizzaro reaction (conc. NaOH giving an alcohol and an acid salt) and a single cross-aldol product both point to an aromatic aldehyde with no $\alpha$-hydrogen.
4-Methoxybenzaldehyde, $\mathrm{CH_3OC_6H_4CHO}$, is $\mathrm{C_8H_8O_2}$ and gives 4-methoxybenzyl alcohol.
(4-Hydroxybenzaldehyde is $\mathrm{C_7H_6O_2}$; 2-hydroxyacetophenone has $\alpha$-hydrogens; 4-methylbenzoic acid is not an aldehyde.)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
3, 3-Dimethyl-2-butanol cannot be prepared by :
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Target: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C{-}CH(OH){-}CH_3}$.
A: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CCHO}$ with $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}$ gives it directly.
B: the alkene is 3,3-dimethylpent-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}C(CH_3)_2{-}CH_2CH_3}$, a $\mathrm{C_7}$ compound; its acid-catalysed hydration (with carbocation rearrangement) gives $\mathrm{C_7}$ alcohols, not the $\mathrm{C_6}$ target. Cannot.
C: ozonolysis of $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C(CH_3)C{=}C(CH_3)C(CH_3)_3}$ gives two molecules of $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CCOCH_3}$, which $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ reduces to the target.
D: $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ reduces $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CCOCH_3}$ to the target.
E: hydration of $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CC{\equiv}CH}$ gives the ketone $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CCOCH_3}$, not the alcohol. Cannot.
Answer: B and E only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The final product [B] is :
questions.sol:
Benzoylation (Schotten-Baumann) of cyclohexylmethylamine gives the amide A, $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}CH_2NHCOC_6H_5}$.
$\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ reduces the amide C=O to $\mathrm{CH_2}$, giving the secondary amine B, $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}CH_2NHCH_2C_6H_5}$ (N-benzyl-1-cyclohexylmethanamine): the fourth structure.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
Reaction of Glucose with		List - II
Product formed
A. HydroxylamineI. Gluconic acid
B. $\mathrm{Br_2}$ waterII. Glucose pentacetate
C. Excess acetic anhydrideIII. Saccharic acid
D. Concentrated $\mathrm{HNO_3}$IV. Glucoxime
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Hydroxylamine reacts with the aldehyde group: glucoxime (A-IV).
Bromine water oxidises only the CHO group: gluconic acid (B-I).
Excess acetic anhydride acetylates all five OH groups: glucose pentaacetate (C-II).
Nitric acid oxidises both the CHO and the terminal $\mathrm{CH_2OH}$: saccharic (glucaric) acid (D-III).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: If the enthalpy of sublimation of Li is 155 kJ mol$^{-1}$, enthalpy of dissociation of $\mathrm{F_2}$ is 150 kJ mol$^{-1}$, ionization enthalpy of Li is 520 kJ mol$^{-1}$, electron gain enthalpy of F is $-313$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, standard enthalpy of formation of LiF is $-594$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. The magnitude of lattice enthalpy of LiF is __________ kJ mol$^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer)
questions.sol:
Born-Haber cycle: $\Delta_fH=\Delta_{\text{sub}}H+IE+\dfrac12\Delta_{\text{diss}}H+\Delta_{eg}H-\Delta_{\text{lattice}}H$ (lattice enthalpy taken for breaking the lattice).
$-594=155+520+75-313-\Delta_{\text{lattice}}H\Rightarrow\Delta_{\text{lattice}}H=437+594=1031$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following electrochemical cell :
$\mathrm{Pt\,|\,O_2(g)(1bar)\,|\,HCl(aq)\,||\,M^{2+}(aq, 1.0M)\,|\,M(s)}$
The pH above which, oxygen gas would start to evolve at anode is __________ (nearest integer).
[Given : $E^\circ_{\mathrm{M^{2+}/M}}=0.994$ V, $E^\circ_{\mathrm{O_2/H_2O}}=1.23$ V (standard reduction potential) and $\dfrac{RT}{F}(2.303)=0.059$ V at the given condition]
questions.sol:
Anode: $\mathrm{2H_2O\to O_2+4H^++4e^-}$, with $E_{\mathrm{O_2/H_2O}}=1.23-0.059\,\text{pH}$ (for 1 bar $\mathrm{O_2}$).
The cell works spontaneously (oxygen evolves) when $E_{\text{cell}}=0.994-(1.23-0.059\,\text{pH})>0$.
$0.059\,\text{pH}>0.236\Rightarrow\text{pH}>4$.

questions.text: Consider $\mathrm{A\xrightarrow{k_1}B}$ and $\mathrm{C\xrightarrow{k_2}D}$ are two reactions. If the rate constant ($k_1$) of the $\mathrm{A\longrightarrow B}$ reaction can be expressed by the following equation $\log_{10}k=14.34-\dfrac{1.5\times10^4}{T/K}$ and activation energy of $\mathrm{C\longrightarrow D}$ reaction ($Ea_2$) is $\dfrac15$th of the $\mathrm{A\longrightarrow B}$ reaction ($Ea_1$), then the value of ($Ea_2$) is __________ kJ mol$^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer)
questions.sol:
Comparing with $\log k=\log A-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303RT}$: $\dfrac{E_{a1}}{2.303R}=1.5\times10^4$ K.
$E_{a1}=1.5\times10^4\times2.303\times8.314\approx2.872\times10^5$ J mol$^{-1}=287.2$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
$E_{a2}=\dfrac{287.2}{5}\approx57$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.

questions.text:
Among the following oxides of 3d elements, the number of mixed oxides are __________.
$\mathrm{Ti_2O_3}$, $\mathrm{V_2O_4}$, $\mathrm{Cr_2O_3}$, $\mathrm{Mn_3O_4}$, $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$, $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$, $\mathrm{Co_3O_4}$
questions.sol:
A mixed oxide contains the metal in two oxidation states.
$\mathrm{Mn_3O_4}$ (MnO$\cdot$Mn$_2$O$_3$), $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$ (FeO$\cdot$Fe$_2$O$_3$) and $\mathrm{Co_3O_4}$ (CoO$\cdot$Co$_2$O$_3$) are mixed oxides.
$\mathrm{Ti_2O_3}$, $\mathrm{Cr_2O_3}$, $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$ (+3) and $\mathrm{V_2O_4}$ (+4) have a single oxidation state. Answer: 3.

questions.text:
The mass of benzanilide obtained from the benzoylation reaction of 5.8 g of aniline, if yield of product is 82%, is __________ g (nearest integer).
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16)
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2+C_6H_5COCl\to C_6H_5NHCOC_6H_5+HCl}$ (1 : 1).
Aniline: $\dfrac{5.8}{93}\approx0.0624$ mol; benzanilide $\mathrm{C_{13}H_{11}NO}$, $M=197$.
Mass $=0.0624\times197\times0.82\approx10.1$ g, i.e. $10$ g.
